open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-004 request decoding
open_points.text: “an import or request carrying its own status or project facts is refused at decoding” does not define “project facts”, although SnapshotPublication and ProjectAuthorizationRequest necessarily carry project_id.
open_points.question: Which caller-supplied fields are forbidden Registry context, and which required identifiers or business facts may a request carry?
options: Only Registry-owned context such as status, display name, address and customer_ref is forbidden; project_id remains allowed.
Every caller-supplied project fact, potentially including project_id, triggers decoding refusal.
open_points.default_guess: Forbid Registry-owned descriptive and lifecycle context but allow the typed project_id required to select the project.

witness.initial: A producer has a valid credential and an active Registry project UUID.
events: The producer submits a SnapshotPublication containing its required project_id and no status, display name, address or customer_ref.
outcomes: The decoder accepts project_id, and the server asks Registry for authoritative context.
The decoder treats project_id as a caller-carried project fact and refuses the publication before any Registry call.
witness.observer: The producer and the Registry gateway

open_points.subject: completed_work_total with no progress records
open_points.text: A9 says a section without progress has completed_work_value None and must not look like zero, while State 1 declares completed_work_total: Decimal and defines it as the sum of non-None section values; an empty such sum is zero.
open_points.question: When an active budget has sections but none has a progress record, is project-level completed_work_total zero or unavailable?
options: Return Decimal 0 as the empty sum.
Represent the total as unavailable/None so absence of all progress is not shown as zero.
open_points.default_guess: Represent it as unavailable until at least one section has recorded progress.

witness.initial: An active budget contains two sections with positive work_planned and neither has a SectionProgress record.
events: A viewer reads BudgetView, ProgressView or PaymentSummaryView.
outcomes: Both section values are None, but completed_work_total is Decimal 0.
Both section values and the aggregate completed-work total are unavailable.

open_points.subject: source-supplied timestamp input and normalization
open_points.text: Source times are “the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC” and the test says they are “stored as supplied”, but “their accepted forms and checks” are carried to States 6–7.
open_points.question: Which supplied datetime representations are accepted, and does “stored as supplied” mean preserving fields or preserving the instant while converting to offset-naive UTC?
options: Accept offset-aware datetimes and convert the same instant to offset-naive UTC.
Accept only UTC datetimes and reject non-UTC offsets.
Accept offset-naive values and interpret them as UTC.
Preserve the supplied wall-clock fields while removing the offset.
open_points.default_guess: Accept datetimes that identify an instant, convert that instant to offset-naive UTC, and reject naive inputs whose UTC meaning is not explicit.

events: The stored ProgressPhoto is read later.
outcomes: The input is accepted and stored as 2026-11-08T10:00:00 with no offset, preserving the instant.
The input is rejected because only an already-UTC form is accepted, or is stored as 2026-11-08T12:00:00 with the offset removed under a literal reading of “as supplied”.
witness.observer: The staff caller and gallery reader

open_points.subject: single wall-clock reading and comparison reuse
open_points.text: The rules require one wall-clock reading whose instant supplies both current-time comparisons and portal-owned timestamps, but CLK-001 tests timestamp equality and TTL arithmetic, while CLK-002 counts only elapsed-clock readings.
open_points.question: What Required test must demonstrate that each time-dependent operation reads the wall clock exactly once and reuses that same instant for validity comparisons as well as writes?
options: Use a counting/ticking wall-clock source for every time-dependent operation and assert one read.
Treat equal written timestamps and TTL arithmetic as sufficient even though they cannot observe comparison-time reads.
open_points.default_guess: Use a counting wall-clock source and assert exactly one read per operation, including operations with only one written timestamp.

witness.initial: A staff session expires at 10:00:00.500, and a mutation begins just before that boundary.
events: The operation checks the session at 10:00:00.400.
The implementation reads the wall clock again at 10:00:00.600 to assign its sole event timestamp.
outcomes: With one reused reading, the mutation succeeds and its event timestamp is 10:00:00.400.
With two readings, the mutation still succeeds but stores 10:00:00.600; the stated CLK-001 tests can pass because there is only one portal-owned event timestamp.
witness.observer: An audit or record reader inspecting the mutation time

open_points.subject: clock source contracts for read-only operations
open_points.text: A28 says every part of the portal obtains time from the clock source, including every comparison deciding validity of persisted records, but the stated carry to State 6 covers only “every mutating operation that writes a fresh timestamp”.
open_points.question: Which receiving-state obligation ensures that read-only authentication and authorization operations that compare expires_at also receive the decided clock source rather than choosing an ambient source?
options: Carry every operation performing a current-time comparison to State 6 with an explicit time-source contract.
Carry only timestamp-writing mutations and leave read-only expiry checks to module implementation.
open_points.default_guess: Carry all current-time consumers, including read-only session and credential resolution, with an explicit time-source contract.

witness.initial: A persisted session is at its exact expiry boundary.
events: A caller performs a read-only project request.
The authorization module resolves the session and must obtain now.
outcomes: The resolver uses the handed clock source and deterministically refuses at now = expires_at.
Because no read-operation contract was carried, the resolver chooses an ambient or separately constructed clock and may admit or refuse depending on that reading.

open_points.subject: CLK-002 witness binding
open_points.text: CLK-002 has a Required tests item, but no Required tests line binds CLK-002 to an existing check with a [witness: ...] tag.
open_points.question: Which existing witness check is bound to CLK-002 and asserts its source scan and one-reading viewer-entry requirements?
options: Bind CLK-002 to an existing verification check that performs both required checks.
Add a distinct clock-source verification check and bind CLK-002 to it.
open_points.default_guess: Bind CLK-002 to a dedicated clock-source verification check covering both the source scan and counting-clock viewer-entry behavior.

open_points.subject: remediation of a vulnerable transitive distribution
open_points.text: Transitive libraries “are not pinned”, DEP-002 permits any image with no affected installed distribution, but rule 3 says a vulnerable image is not deployed “until the pin is updated through the Factory route”.
open_points.question: If a vulnerable transitive distribution is replaced by a fixed compatible version when the image is rebuilt with unchanged direct pins, may that new passing image deploy, or must some direct pin still change?
options: The rebuilt passing image may deploy because DEP-002 judges the installed distributions of that image.
A direct pin must change through the Factory route even when the vulnerable transitive version is no longer installed.
The transitive distribution must become an explicit exact pin before deployment.
open_points.default_guess: Allow the newly built image to deploy if its complete installed distribution set passes the fresh OSV check, without requiring an unrelated direct-pin change.

witness.initial: The requirements contain an unchanged exact direct pin P; the built image contains vulnerable transitive distribution T version 1.
events: The deploy is blocked by OSV.
T version 2, which fixes the advisory and remains compatible with P, is released.
A new image is built from the same requirements and resolves T version 2.
The new image passes a fresh OSV check.
outcomes: DEP-002 permits the new image because no installed distribution is affected.
Rule 3 continues to block deployment because no direct pin was updated through the Factory route.
